caption: Tissue identity is the dominant axis of variation across all adult samples.
Splitting the ovary into two compartments reveals no strong proximal or distal ovary identity.
Drosophila housekeeping orthologues behave as housekeeping genes in C. capitata.
Male- and female-biased genes are overwhelmingly germline-specific, with a small set shared with the soma.
Most expressed genes show strong tissue specificity (tau close to 1).
Adult tissues form distinct expression clusters by pairwise correlation.
